title: UNRAVELING INFLUENZA: FROM LABORATORY DIAGNOSIS TO CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL IMPACT
abstract: Introduction: Influenza is an enveloped, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA virus of the Orthomyxoviridae family, classified into types A, B, and C. Seasonal influenza remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality. Objective: To describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of individuals with influenza infection and to assess microbiological findings. Methods: This study analyzed medical records of hospitalized and non-hospitalized individuals of all ages and genders evaluated in a Brazilian public healthcare service. Laboratory-confirmed Influenza cases identified by molecular testing between February 2024 and July 2025 were included. Clinical specimens consisted of nasopharyngeal swabs (n=95) and tracheal aspirates (n=3). Viral RNA was extracted using the KingFisher system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sweden). RT-qPCR assays were performed to detect SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus, and Influenza A/B, including Influenza A typing, using the QuantStudio 5 platform (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sweden). Ct values were recorded for viral load assessment. Clinical and epidemiological variables were analyzed. Results: Influenza A (H1N1) was the most frequently detected subtype (62.3%), followed by non-typed Influenza A (26.5%) and Influenza B (11.2%). Cough was reported in 82.6% of individuals. The most common comorbidities were chronic neurological disease (15.3%) and Down syndrome (11.2%). Influenza vaccination was reported by 17.4% of individuals, while 32.6% had received the COVID-19 vaccine. Antiviral therapy was administered to 6.2% of individuals, 37.8% required ventilatory support, 65.3% were hospitalized, and 34.7% were managed as outpatients. Ct values ≤35 were observed in 91.8% of samples collected within 10 days of symptom onset. Conclusions: The predominance of H1N1 highlights its epidemiological relevance. Expanding vaccination, surveillance, and timely antiviral use is essential to reduce disease severity and healthcare burden.
authors: GIOVANNA DE SOUZA TIBURCIO DA SILVA

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性流感仍然是全球发病率和死亡率的主要原因。本研究旨在描述流感感染个体的临床和流行病学特征,并评估微生物学发现。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了巴西公共医疗服务体系中所有年龄和性别住院及非住院个体的医疗记录。纳入了2024年2月至2025年7月期间通过分子检测确认的流感病例。临床样本包括鼻咽拭子(n=95)和气管吸引物(n=3)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用KingFisher系统(Thermo Fisher Scientific,瑞典)提取病毒RNA。通过QuantStudio 5平台(Thermo Fisher Scientific,瑞典)进行RT-qPCR检测,以检测SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒和流感A/B型,包括流感A型的分型。记录了Ct值以评估病毒载量。分析了临床和流行病学变量。
elements_zh.main_results: 甲型H1N1流感病毒(甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09)是最常检测到的亚型(62.3%),其次是未分型的甲型流感病毒(26.5%)和乙型流感病毒(11.2%)。82.6%的个体报告有咳嗽症状。最常见的合并症是慢性神经系统疾病(15.3%)和唐氏综合征(11.2%)。17.4%的个体报告感染了疫苗接种流感病毒,而32.6%的个体曾接种过COVID-19 疫苗疫苗。在发病后10天内采集的样本中,91.8%的Ct值≤35。6.2%的个体接受了抗病毒药物治疗,37.8%需要机械通气支持,65.3%住院治疗,34.7%作为门诊患者处理。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: H1N1型流感的主导地位突显了其流行病学意义。扩大疫苗接种、监测以及及时使用抗病毒药物治疗对于减轻疾病严重程度和医疗负担至关重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以用于制定针对性的疫苗接种策略,改进监测系统,并及时使用抗病毒药物治疗以减轻季节性流感的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于医疗记录,未包含详细的实验室或统计程序。由于依赖观察性数据且缺乏实验对照,证据强度中等。

title: From detection to prediction: Asymptomatic shedding-informed mass-balance modeling predicts travel-borne viral importation at airports
abstract: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) has emerged as a non-invasive tool for travel-mediated pathogen detection, yet its utility remains largely descriptive without capacity to translate environmental concentrations into quantitative infection dynamics. This study aimed to advance AWS from passive pathogen detection to an active predictive framework by integrating mass balance back-calculation with hybrid-capture genomic surveillance. To resolve a critical parameter gap in mass-balance modeling-namely, the fecal shedding kinetics of asymptomatic influenza carriers, we prospectively enrolled 238 non-respiratory outpatients at Nanchang People's Hospital and quantified fecal influenza A/B virus loads (IAV /IBV) by RT-qPCR. Asymptomatic IAV and IBV shedding was detected across all age strata, with median viral loads of 5.9 and 5.0 log10 copies/g, respectively, and positivity rates ranging from 41.2% (adolescents) to 62.1% (children <10 years), thereby establishing the first empirical fecal shedding parameter set for carriage-inclusive mass-balance back-calculation. Between January and July 2025, we prospectively collected 240 aircraft wastewater samples from six Asia-Pacific flight routes and 60 longitudinal sewage samples from an international airport in Nanjing, China. RT-qPCR was conducted to quantify norovirus, influenza virus, mpox, and dengue virus. A mass balance back-calculation model was established to convert wastewater viral concentrations into estimated weekly numbers of infected inbound passengers. Viral genomes were enriched via hybrid-capture panels and subjected to high-resolution phylogenetic analysis. The predictive framework estimated weekly flight-imported infection cases for norovirus GII, influenza A virus and dengue virus, revealing distinct regional importation curves synchronized with epidemiological trends in countries of origin (95% concordance). Phylogenetic analysis resolved multiple independent viral introductions. Further employing a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered model, we forecasted 14-day community infection burden and validated predictions against clinical surveillance data, demonstrating significant concordance with IAV (r=0.71) and norovirus clinical visits (r=0.84). By bridging quantitative infection dynamics with lineage-resolution genomics, this study establishes a paradigm shift from qualitative pathogen detection to predictive outbreak intelligence.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need to move aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) from passive pathogen detection to an active predictive framework. It focuses on seasonal influenza viruses, specifically influenza A and B, by integrating mass balance back-calculation with hybrid-capture genomic surveillance. The research enrolled 238 non-respiratory outpatients to quantify fecal viral loads, revealing asymptomatic shedding across all age groups with median viral loads of 5.9 and 5.0 log10 copies/g for influenza A and B, respectively. The findings establish the first empirical fecal shedding parameter set for mass-balance modeling. The study also collected wastewater samples from six Asia-Pacific flight routes and validated predictions against clinical surveillance data, showing significant concordance with influenza A virus and norovirus. The results demonstrate the potential of AWS to predict travel-borne viral importation and provide insights into outbreak intelligence. However, the study's predictive framework is limited to the context of the collected data and does not extend to other viruses without explicit target-specific evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 航空废水(AWS)已成为一种非侵入性的旅行媒介病原体检测工具,但其应用仍主要停留在描述性层面,无法将环境浓度转化为定量感染动态。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在通过将质能平衡逆向计算与混合捕获技术相结合,将AWS从被动病原体检测推进到主动预测框架。
elements_zh.methods: 为解决质能平衡建模中的关键参数缺口——即无症状流感携带者的粪便排毒动力学,我们前瞻性地招募了238名非呼吸道门诊患者,并通过RT-qPCR定量检测了粪便中甲型/乙型流感病毒载量(IAV/IBV)。
elements_zh.main_results: 无症状IAV和IBV排毒在所有年龄层中均被检测到,其中中位病毒载量分别为5.9和5.0 log10 copies/g,阳性率从41.2%(青少年)到62.1%(<10岁儿童)不等,从而建立了首个包含携带者在内的质能平衡逆向计算的实证粪便排毒参数集。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该预测框架估计了诺如病毒GII、流感A病毒和登革病毒的每周航班输入感染病例,揭示了与原发国流行趋势同步的区域输入曲线(95%一致性)。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过将定量感染动态与谱系分辨率基因组学相结合,本研究确立了从定性病原体检测向预测性病毒情报转变的新范式。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 进一步采用易感-暴露-感染-恢复(SEIR)模型,我们预测了14天内的社区感染负担,并将预测结果与临床数据进行验证,显示出与IAV(r=0.71)和诺如病毒临床就诊(r=0.84)显著的一致性。

title_zh: 从检测到预测:无症状排毒信息引导的质能平衡建模预测机场传播性病毒输入
source_body_en: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) has emerged as a non-invasive tool for travel-mediated pathogen detection, yet its utility remains largely descriptive without capacity to translate environmental concentrations into quantitative infection dynamics. This study aimed to advance AWS from passive pathogen detection to an active predictive framework by integrating mass balance back-calculation with hybrid-capture genomic surveillance. To resolve a critical parameter gap in mass-balance modeling-namely, the fecal shedding kinetics of asymptomatic influenza carriers, we prospectively enrolled 238 non-respiratory outpatients at Nanchang People's Hospital and quantified fecal influenza A/B virus loads (IAV /IBV) by RT-qPCR. Asymptomatic IAV and IBV shedding was detected across all age strata, with median viral loads of 5.9 and 5.0 log10 copies/g, respectively, and positivity rates ranging from 41.2% (adolescents) to 62.1% (children <10 years), thereby establishing the first empirical fecal shedding parameter set for carriage-inclusive mass-balance back-calculation. Between January and July 2025, we prospectively collected 240 aircraft wastewater samples from six Asia-Pacific flight routes and 60 longitudinal sewage samples from an international airport in Nanjing, China. RT-qPCR was conducted to quantify norovirus, influenza virus, mpox, and dengue virus. A mass balance back-calculation model was established to convert wastewater viral concentrations into estimated weekly numbers of infected inbound passengers. Viral genomes were enriched via hybrid-capture panels and subjected to high-resolution phylogenetic analysis. The predictive framework estimated weekly flight-imported infection cases for norovirus GII, influenza A virus and dengue virus, revealing distinct regional importation curves synchronized with epidemiological trends in countries of origin (95% concordance). Phylogenetic analysis resolved multiple independent viral introductions. Further employing a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered model, we forecasted 14-day community infection burden and validated predictions against clinical surveillance data, demonstrating significant concordance with IAV (r=0.71) and norovirus clinical visits (r=0.84). By bridging quantitative infection dynamics with lineage-resolution genomics, this study establishes a paradigm shift from qualitative pathogen detection to predictive outbreak intelligence.
abstract_zh: 航空废水(AWS)已成为一种非侵入性的旅行媒介病原体检测工具,但其应用仍主要停留在描述性层面,无法将环境浓度转化为定量感染动态。本研究旨在通过将质能平衡逆向计算与混合捕获技术相结合,将AWS从被动病原体检测推进到主动预测框架。为解决质能平衡建模中的关键参数缺口——即无症状流感携带者的粪便排毒动力学,我们前瞻性地招募了238名非呼吸道门诊患者,并通过RT-qPCR定量检测了粪便中甲型/乙型流感病毒载量(IAV/IBV)。无症状IAV和IBV排毒在所有年龄层中均被检测到,其中中位病毒载量分别为5.9和5.0 log10 copies/g,阳性率从41.2%(青少年)到62.1%(<10岁儿童)不等,从而建立了首个包含携带者在内的质能平衡逆向计算的实证粪便排毒参数集。2025年1月至7月期间,我们前瞻性地从六个亚太航线收集了240份航空废水样本,并从中国南京的国际机场收集了60份纵向污水样本。通过RT-qPCR对诺如病毒、流感病毒、猴痘病毒和登革病毒进行了定量检测。建立了一个质能平衡逆向计算模型,将废水中的病毒浓度转化为估计的每周入境感染乘客数量。病毒通过混合捕获面板进行富集,并进行高分辨率系统发育分析。该预测框架估计了诺如病毒GII、流感A病毒和登革病毒的每周航班输入感染病例,揭示了与原发国流行趋势同步的区域输入曲线(95%一致性)。系统发育分析明确了多个独立的病毒输入事件。进一步采用易感-暴露-感染-恢复(SEIR)模型,我们预测了14天内的社区感染负担,并将预测结果与临床数据进行验证,显示出与IAV(r=0.71)和诺如病毒临床就诊(r=0.84)显著的一致性。通过将定量感染动态与谱系分辨率基因组学相结合,本研究确立了从定性病原体检测向预测性病毒情报转变的新范式。

title: H1N1 preimmunity improves antibody responses to vaccination and alters draining lymph node germinal center signatures
abstract: Influenza viruses circulate annually in humans, accumulating mutations in the viral genome. In real-world conditions, people develop an immune history from multiple influenza virus infections and vaccinations, yet most experimental studies utilize naïve hosts to investigate viral pathogenesis or vaccine efficacy; a scenario that does not reflect actual human exposure and immune responses. Here, we report that mice previously infected with the mouse-adapted H1N1 virus mounted an increased antibody response after vaccination with the split virion quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine. Antibodies targeting the H1 antigen component of the vaccine in H1N1 preimmune mice had titers peaking at a log 2 HAI titer of 8 versus 2 in naïve-vaccinated mice at 14 days post-vaccination, whereas H3N2 pre-immune mice showed no improved vaccine responses. Increased total serum class-switched IgG subclass concentrations in the H1N1 preimmune-vaccinated mice accompanied protection from weight loss and mortality when these mice were challenged with an H1N1 pandemic 2009 strain. Temporal sampling and analysis of RNA from mediastinal lymph nodes from preimmune mice by RNA-seq at time points following vaccination revealed distinct regulation of lymphocyte and germinal center-specific genes, including Bcl6 , an essential gene for germinal-center-dependent B-cells. Taken together, H1N1 A/FM/1/1947 preimmunity led to a more efficient vaccine response accompanied by altered expression of germinal center-associated genes in the mediastinal lymph node, with implications for future vaccine design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza viruses circulate annually in humans, accumulating mutations in the viral genome. The study aimed to investigate how prior immunity to H1N1 affects vaccine responses in real-world conditions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved mice previously infected with the mouse-adapted H1N1 virus and compared their responses to vaccination with naïve mice. It was conducted in a controlled laboratory setting using mice as the host.
analysis.methods: The researchers vaccinated mice with the split virion quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine and measured antibody titers against the H1 antigen. They also analyzed RNA from mediastinal lymph nodes using RNA-seq to assess gene expression changes.
analysis.main_results: H1N1 preimmune mice exhibited higher antibody titers against the H1 antigen, peaking at a log 2 HAI titer of 8 compared to 2 in naïve-vaccinated mice at 14 days post-vaccination. H3N2 pre-immune mice showed no improved vaccine responses. Increased total serum class-switched IgG subclass concentrations in H1N1 preimmune-vaccinated mice were observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that prior H1N1 infection enhances vaccine efficacy by increasing antibody titers and altering germinal center gene expression, which may inform future vaccine design.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results have implications for understanding how preexisting immunity influences vaccine effectiveness, potentially guiding the development of more efficient influenza vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used mice as a model, which may not fully reflect human immune responses. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on animal models and does not include human data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how prior immunity to H1N1 influences vaccine responses in mice. It reports that H1N1 preimmune mice showed increased antibody titers and altered germinal center gene expression after vaccination, suggesting potential implications for vaccine design. The study used a mouse model and compared vaccinated preimmune and naïve mice. While the results are promising, the findings are limited to animal models and do not include human data, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及先前感染过鼠源适应型H1N1病毒的小鼠,并将其与未感染小鼠进行比较,以评估其对疫苗接种的反应。研究在受控的实验室环境中进行,使用小鼠作为宿主。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用四价裂解病毒颗粒季节性流感 疫苗对小鼠进行疫苗接种,并测量其对H1抗原的抗体滴度。他们还通过RNA测序分析纵隔淋巴结中的RNA,以评估基因表达的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: H1N1前免疫小鼠对H1抗原的抗体滴度更高,在接种疫苗接种后14天达到log 2 HAI滴度8,而未感染接种小鼠的滴度仅为2。H3N2前免疫小鼠未表现出改善的疫苗反应。在H1N1前免疫接种小鼠中,观察到总血清类转换IgG亚类浓度增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,先前的H1N1感染通过增加抗体滴度和改变生发中心基因表达来增强疫苗的效果,这可能为未来疫苗的设计提供参考。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于理解先前免疫力如何影响疫苗的效果,可能指导开发更有效的流感疫苗。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究使用小鼠作为模型,这可能无法完全反映人类免疫应答。由于基于动物模型且未包括人类数据,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 流感病毒在人类中每年循环传播,积累突变于病毒基因组中。在现实条件下,人们通过多次流感病毒感染和疫苗接种形成免疫历史,但大多数实验研究使用未感染的宿主来研究病毒发病机制或疫苗的效果;这种情景无法反映实际的人类暴露和免疫应答。在这里,我们报告称,先前感染过鼠源适应型H1N1病毒的小鼠在接种疫苗接种后,对四价裂解病毒颗粒季节性流感 疫苗的抗体反应增强。在H1N1前免疫小鼠中,针对疫苗中H1抗原组分的抗体滴度在接种疫苗接种后14天达到log 2 HAI滴度8,而未感染接种小鼠的滴度仅为2。相比之下,H3N2前免疫小鼠未表现出改善的疫苗反应。在H1N1前免疫接种小鼠中,总血清类转换IgG亚类浓度增加,这些小鼠在被H1N1大流行2009株感染时表现出对体重减轻和死亡率的保护作用。通过在接种疫苗接种后不同时间点对前免疫小鼠的纵隔淋巴结进行RNA测序分析,研究人员发现淋巴细胞和生发中心特异性基因的调控存在显著差异,包括Bcl6,这是依赖生发中心的B细胞的关键基因。综上所述,H1N1 A/FM/1/1947前免疫导致了更有效的疫苗反应,并伴随纵隔淋巴结中与生发中心相关的基因表达改变,这可能对未来疫苗的设计产生影响。

title: INFLUENZA VIRUS CIRCULATION DURING 2024-2025 SEASON IN RABAT, MOROCCO
abstract: Introduction: Influenza remains a major cause of respiratory morbidity worldwide. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that seasonal influenza epidemic is responsible for millions of severe infections and hundreds of thousands of deaths each year. Global surveillance of influenza viruses is coordinated via the World Health Organization Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS). The organization follows circulating influenza virus on all continents and provides relevant information for vaccine strain selection as well as public health considerations. This study describes the circulation patterns of influenza viruses at Mohammed V Military Teaching Hospital (MVMTH) in Rabat during the 2024-2025 Influenza season. Methods: A prospective observational study was conducted from October 2024 to March 2025. Nasopharyngeal swabs from patients with influenza-like illness were analyzed using RT-PCR (Film Array Respiratory Panel and GeneXpert Xpress Flu/RSV). Results: Influenza A viruses showed up in most of the tested samples. Among influenza A viruses, viral A(H1N1)pdm09 infection was detected the most commonly. Influenza B viruses were also recorded but circulated at lower levels during the surveillance period. One hundred and sixteen cases were confirmed. Influenza A predominated (80%; n=93), while Influenza B accounted for 20% (n=23). Among Type A cases, A(H1N1)pd2009 was the primary subtype identified (64.5%; n=60), followed by non-subtyped strains (35.5%; n=33). A(H3N2) circulation was marginal (2.8%). Temporally, A(H1N1) peaked in week 4 of 2025, whereas Influenza B showed dominant activity in the late season (Weeks 14-17). Conclusion: The 2024-2025 season was characterized by the dominance of Influenza A(H1N1) and a late-season shift to Influenza B. These findings highlight the necessity of local surveillance to optimize hospital resource allocation and vaccination timing in Morocco.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Influenza virus research in an era of emerging respiratory threats: host–virus interactions, surveillance technologies, antiviral management and resistance, and vaccine preparedness
abstract: Seasonal epidemics, zoonotic spillover, antiviral resistance, and pandemic risk continue to make influenza a major challenge for respiratory preparedness. The recent spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in mammalian hosts has made it increasingly important to consider molecular adaptation, surveillance, treatment, and vaccination as connected parts of preparedness rather than as separate issues. This review focuses on four interconnected areas: host–virus interactions, surveillance technologies, antiviral management and resistance, and vaccine preparedness. Evidence on mammalian adaptation includes receptor specificity, viral polymerase–host factor compatibility, innate immune antagonism, ANP32 proteins, and aberrant viral RNA generation, while surveillance has expanded to multiplex and CRISPR-based assays, point-of-care platforms, genomic sequencing, artificial intelligence-assisted risk assessment, and environmental monitoring. These approaches differ in intended use and stage of validation. Antiviral benefit depends strongly on host risk and treatment timing. Resistance-associated substitutions, however, cannot be interpreted from sequence data alone and require phenotypic and epidemiological context. Vaccine development spans nanoparticle, mRNA, and intranasal platforms designed to broaden antigenic coverage, strengthen mucosal immunity, or improve protection in specific populations. Better analytical performance and stronger immune responses do not by themselves demonstrate reductions in severe disease, hospitalization, or mortality. Influenza preparedness ultimately depends on how effectively these four domains inform one another and how consistently emerging approaches are evaluated against clinically meaningful outcomes.

title: Influenza Virus Antigenic Drift: Balancing Fitness and Immune Evasion
abstract: Human influenza viruses demonstrate immense antigenic variability as a strategy to evade host immunity. The process of evolving to evade host antibody responses, known as antigenic drift, allows influenza viruses to evade epitope-specific antibodies, leading to seasonal influenza outbreaks. Neutralizing antibodies, the major drivers of antigenic drift, target a wide range of epitopes in hemagglutinin and neuraminidase, including functionally conserved regions. In this review, we describe antibody targets of influenza viruses, how influenza viruses have evolved to evade these antibody specificities, and how epistasis helps maintain viral fitness. Then we discuss emerging approaches to study and predict antigenic drift that may improve strain selection for seasonal influenza vaccines.

title_zh: 流感病毒抗原漂移:平衡适应性与免疫逃逸
source_body_en: Human influenza viruses demonstrate immense antigenic variability as a strategy to evade host immunity. The process of evolving to evade host antibody responses, known as antigenic drift, allows influenza viruses to evade epitope-specific antibodies, leading to seasonal influenza outbreaks. Neutralizing antibodies, the major drivers of antigenic drift, target a wide range of epitopes in hemagglutinin and neuraminidase, including functionally conserved regions. In this review, we describe antibody targets of influenza viruses, how influenza viruses have evolved to evade these antibody specificities, and how epistasis helps maintain viral fitness. Then we discuss emerging approaches to study and predict antigenic drift that may improve strain selection for seasonal influenza vaccines.
abstract_zh: 人类流感病毒通过巨大的抗原变异作为策略来逃避宿主免疫。进化以逃避宿主抗体反应的过程,称为抗原漂移,使流感病毒能够逃避表位特异性抗体,导致季节性流感 暴发。中和抗体是抗原漂移的主要驱动力,它们针对血凝素和神经氨酸酶中的多种表位,包括功能保守区域。在本综述中,我们描述了流感病毒的抗体靶点,流感病毒如何进化以逃避这些抗体特异性,以及表型互作如何帮助维持病毒适应性。然后我们讨论了研究和预测抗原漂移的新方法,这些方法可能有助于改进季节性流感 疫苗的毒株选择。

title: Förster Resonance Energy Transfer-Based Selective Detection of Influenza Viruses Using N-Doped Sialic Acid Carbon Dots.
abstract: We report the rational design and synthesis of nitrogen-doped sialic acid-derived carbon dots (SiaMPDA CDs) with excitation-independent green emission and high quantum yield and demonstrate their application as efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) donors for the selective detection of influenza A virus (IAV) subtypes. The surface functionalization of the CDs with sialic acid moieties enables specific molecular recognition of the viral hemagglutinin (HA) protein via multivalent hydrogen-bonding interactions. In combination with Rhodamine B (RhB) as an acceptor, the SiaMPDA-RhB pair exhibits efficient FRET under native conditions. Upon interaction with IAV (H3N2 and H1N1), the FRET system displays anomalous spectral behavior characterized by a simultaneous increase in both donor and acceptor emission intensities without any spectral shift. Mechanistic investigations suggest the formation of a ternary IAV-SiaMPDA-RhB complex, wherein long-range charge transfer coupled with FRET governs the observed fluorescence response. Control experiments with proteins, membrane vesicles, and liposomes confirm that the signal specificity arises from targeted interactions between the sialic acid functionalities of the CDs and the viral surface proteins. The sensing platform enables selective and sensitive detection of IAV subtypes in the picomolar range, comparable to existing carbon dot-based detection systems. These findings establish N-doped sialic acid carbon dots as promising nanoscale probes for virus detection and provide insights into charge-transfer-coupled FRET mechanisms in complex bionano interfaces.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the design, synthesis, and application of nitrogen-doped sialic acid-derived carbon dots (SiaMPDA CDs) as FRET donors for detecting influenza A virus subtypes, specifically H3N2 and H1N1, in controlled experimental conditions.
analysis.methods: The researchers synthesized SiaMPDA CDs and functionalized their surface with sialic acid moieties to enable specific molecular recognition of the viral hemagglutinin (HA) protein through multivalent hydrogen-bonding interactions. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a promising platform for selective and sensitive detection of influenza A subtypes, which could enhance surveillance and diagnostic capabilities for seasonal influenza viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel sensing platform using nitrogen-doped sialic acid-derived carbon dots (SiaMPDA CDs) for the selective detection of influenza A virus subtypes, specifically H3N2 and H1N1. The SiaMPDA CDs are functionalized with sialic acid moieties to enable specific molecular recognition of the viral hemagglutinin (HA) protein through multivalent hydrogen-bonding interactions. When combined with Rhodamine B (RhB) as an acceptor, the system exhibits efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) under native conditions. Upon interaction with IAV subtypes, the FRET system shows anomalous spectral behavior with increased donor and acceptor emission intensities without spectral shift. Mechanistic investigations suggest the formation of a ternary complex involving IAV, SiaMPDA, and RhB, where long-range charge transfer and FRET govern the fluorescence response. Control experiments confirm the signal specificity arises from targeted interactions between the sialic acid functionalities and viral surface proteins. The platform enables detection in the picomolar range, comparable to existing carbon dot-based systems. title_zh: 基于福斯特共振能量转移的流感病毒选择性检测方法:使用氮掺杂唾液酸碳点
source_body_en: We report the rational design and synthesis of nitrogen-doped sialic acid-derived carbon dots (SiaMPDA CDs) with excitation-independent green emission and high quantum yield and demonstrate their application as efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) donors for the selective detection of influenza A virus (IAV) subtypes. The surface functionalization of the CDs with sialic acid moieties enables specific molecular recognition of the viral hemagglutinin (HA) protein via multivalent hydrogen-bonding interactions. In combination with Rhodamine B (RhB) as an acceptor, the SiaMPDA-RhB pair exhibits efficient FRET under native conditions. Upon interaction with IAV (H3N2 and H1N1), the FRET system displays anomalous spectral behavior characterized by a simultaneous increase in both donor and acceptor emission intensities without any spectral shift. Mechanistic investigations suggest the formation of a ternary IAV-SiaMPDA-RhB complex, wherein long-range charge transfer coupled with FRET governs the observed fluorescence response. Control experiments with proteins, membrane vesicles, and liposomes confirm that the signal specificity arises from targeted interactions between the sialic acid functionalities of the CDs and the viral surface proteins. The sensing platform enables selective and sensitive detection of IAV subtypes in the picomolar range, comparable to existing carbon dot-based detection systems. These findings establish N-doped sialic acid carbon dots as promising nanoscale probes for virus detection and provide insights into charge-transfer-coupled FRET mechanisms in complex bionano interfaces.
abstract_zh: 我们报告了氮掺杂唾液酸衍生碳点(SiaMPDA CDs)的合理设计与合成,这些碳点具有与激发波长无关的绿色发射和高量子产率,并展示了其作为高效福斯特共振能量转移(FRET)供体用于流感A病毒(IAV)亚型选择性检测的应用。通过在碳点表面引入唾液酸基团,使其能够通过多价氢键相互作用特异性识别病毒血凝素(HA)蛋白。在与罗丹明B(RhB)作为受体结合后,SiaMPDA-RhB对在天然条件下表现出高效的FRET。当与IAV(H3N2和H1N1)相互作用时,FRET系统表现出异常的光谱行为,特征是供体和受体发射强度同时增加,而没有光谱位移。机制研究提示形成了一个三元IAV-SiaMPDA-RhB复合物,其中长程电荷转移与FRET共同调控所观察到的荧光响应。与蛋白质、膜囊泡和脂质体进行的对照实验确认,信号特异性来源于碳点唾液酸功能团与病毒表面蛋白之间的靶向相互作用。该传感平台能够选择性且灵敏地检测IAV亚型,在皮摩尔范围内,其性能与现有的碳点基检测系统相当。这些发现确立了氮掺杂唾液酸碳点作为病毒检测的有前景的纳米探针,并提供了对复杂生物纳米界面中电荷转移耦合FRET机制的见解。

title: Spatiotemporal clustering of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 at the wild waterfowl-poultry interface: Vector-specific spillover risks in the U.S., 2022–2025
abstract: The emergence of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in North America, beginning in February 2022, has highlighted the dynamic, unpredictable, and regionally variable risk of infections. Studies are needed to assess the spatiotemporal clustering of HPAI H5 at the interface between wild waterfowl and commercial poultry to better understand and mitigate this risk. Publicly available data on HPAI H5 detections in wild birds and commercial poultry from January 2022 to January 2026 were analyzed at the county level. Retrospective space-time permutation models were used to identify and scan for clusters with higher-than-expected detection rates. A total of 17,091 HPAI H5 detections were reported in wild birds across 1,467 county-level locations. Four species, Mallard ( Anas platyrhynchos ) (2,848 detections, 16.66%), Canada goose ( Branta canadensis ) (1,496, 8.75%), Green-winged teal ( Anas carolinensis ) (1,364, 7.98%), and Snow goose ( Anser caerulescens ) (1,084, 6.34%), accounted for 39.73% of detections. In commercial poultry, 532 outbreaks in turkey operations, 148 outbreaks in table-egg layer operations, 99 outbreaks in broiler chicken operations, and 89 outbreaks in commercial duck operations were reported, respectively. Several spillover events followed an east-to-west expansion. In early 2022, mallard detections preceded outbreaks in Northeast egg-layer and duck farms, while snow goose detections in the Upper Midwest coincided with turkey farm outbreaks. In the Pacific and Mountain West during summer 2022, detections in Canada geese overlapped with turkey farm outbreaks. A resurgence occurred in the Midwest (2025), with snow and Canada goose detections overlapping severe outbreaks in turkey and layer flocks. Additionally, in the Upper Midwest, Canada goose and mallard detections overlapped with outbreaks in commercial duck farms during fall-winter 2025. The study findings demonstrate distinct vector-based transmission dynamics of HPAI H5 at the wild waterfowl-poultry interface. Farm biosecurity strategies must adapt to these recurrent, vector-specific risks.

title: Co-infection models of Staphylococcus aureus and respiratory viruses reveal synergistic interactions counteracted by a bithiazole derivative
abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infections represent a major contributor to global morbidity and mortality. In influenza virus infections, secondary bacterial pneumonia occurs in approximately 20–30% of cases and is associated with an increased risk of shock, mechanical ventilation, and even mortality. Bacterial superinfections are frequent causes of mortality in influenza severe infections and have been a major cause of morbidity and mortality also in COVID-19 patients. Staphylococcus aureus has been identified as one of the most prevalent bacterial pathogens among hospitalized and non-hospitalized patients who have tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 or influenza virus infections. Generally, antibiotic therapy is administered to at-risk patients to preclude bacterial over-infections by eliminating susceptible pathogens, increasing selective pressure favoring antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Due to the recognized public health problem of antibiotic resistance, the exploration of alternative therapies to counteract or prevent the development of serious virus/bacteria co-infections has become a critical research priority. The present study aimed to investigate the interactions between coronavirus or influenza A virus, and S. aureus in a co-infection model and to investigate the ability of a known antiviral/antibacterial compound, the bithiazole derivative MR335, to counteract the interaction between the two pathogens. The co-infection models were established using the pulmonary cell line A549 and the bronchial cell line BEAS-2B. The synergistic interaction between virus and bacteria were assessed through standard viral titration assays and bacterial adhesion and invasion assays. The bithiazole compound, MR335, showed both antiviral and antibacterial activity at distinct concentrations. In particular, it effectively counteracted the synergistic interactions between respiratory viruses and S. aureus at concentration that retained antiviral but not antibacterial activity. Notably, eradication of viruses impaired bacterial invasion, suggesting their synergistic cooperation and opening the way to alternative therapies that prevent bacterial superinfection without resorting to conventional antibiotics.
journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 病毒-细菌共感染是全球发病率和死亡率的重要因素。预防细菌过度感染的抗生素治疗会增加选择压力,促进抗生素耐药细菌的生长,凸显了寻找替代疗法的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在通过肺和支气管细胞系建立共感染模型,研究冠状病毒或流感A病毒与金黄色葡萄球菌之间的相互作用,并评估二噻唑衍生物MR335对抗这些相互作用的能力。
elements_zh.methods: 通过标准病毒滴度测定和细菌黏附与侵入实验评估病毒与细菌之间的协同作用。二噻唑化合物MR335在不同浓度下表现出抗病毒活性和抗菌活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 二噻唑化合物MR335在保留抗病毒活性但不具有抗菌活性的浓度下,有效抵消了呼吸道病毒与金黄色葡萄球菌之间的协同作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究证明MR335能够抵消呼吸道病毒与金黄色葡萄球菌之间的协同作用,表明其可能作为替代疗法,用于预防细菌继发感染,而无需依赖传统抗生素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发新的疗法,以预防严重的病毒/细菌共感染,从而应对抗生素耐药性的公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究设计的局限性,包括使用细胞系,可能会影响结果的普遍适用性。由于证据仅基于摘要,其证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究证明MR335能够抵消呼吸道病毒与金黄色葡萄球菌之间的协同作用,表明其可能作为替代疗法,用于预防细菌继发感染,而无需依赖传统抗生素。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发新的疗法,以预防严重的病毒/细菌共感染,从而应对抗生素耐药性的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究设计的局限性,包括使用细胞系,可能会影响结果的普遍适用性。由于证据仅基于摘要,其证据强度中等。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the one-year mortality rate among adults hospitalized with seasonal influenza viruses in Southern Sweden, addressing the public health concern of understanding long-term outcomes following severe influenza infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a retrospective observational study conducted in Southern Sweden between 2010 and 2020, focusing on adults hospitalized with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or B viruses.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed medical records of adults admitted to intensive care units with confirmed influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or B infections, using a retrospective observational approach to evaluate one-year mortality rates.
analysis.main_results: The study reported a high one-year mortality rate of 30% among adults with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or B viruses who required intensive care.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high mortality rate as indicative of the severity of influenza infections in adults requiring intensive care, highlighting the need for improved surveillance and management strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of monitoring long-term outcomes in patients with severe seasonal influenza, informing future research and public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential biases in data collection, but the evidence is strong due to the clear focus on the target influenza viruses and the use of medical records from a well-defined region.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational study investigated the one-year mortality rate among adults hospitalized with seasonal influenza viruses in Southern Sweden. The study focused on influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B viruses, reporting a high mortality rate of 30% among those requiring intensive care. The authors interpreted these findings as highlighting the severity of influenza infections in this population, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and management. The study's limitations include its retrospective nature and potential biases, but the evidence is considered strong due to the clear focus on the target viruses and the use of medical records from a defined region. The results have significant implications for understanding long-term outcomes in severe influenza cases and could inform future public health strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是一项在南方瑞典2010年至2020年间进行的回顾性观察研究,关注感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒的成人住院患者。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究分析了接受重症监护的成人患者医疗记录,这些患者被确诊感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒,采用回顾性观察方法评估一年内的死亡率发生率。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究报告称,接受重症监护的感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒的成人患者中,一年内的死亡率发生率高达30%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将高死亡率发生率解释为成人重症监护患者中流感感染严重性的指标,强调了改进监测和管理策略的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现突显了对严重季节性流感患者进行长期结果监测的重要性,为未来的研究和公共卫生干预提供了依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究采用回顾性设计,且数据收集可能存在偏倚,因此存在一定的局限性;但证据强度较高,因为研究明确聚焦于目标流感病毒,并使用了定义明确地区的医疗记录。}}.{

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估南方瑞典住院成人患者中感染季节性流感病毒后一年的死亡率发生率,以应对了解严重流感感染长期结果的公共卫生关切。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是一项在南方瑞典2010年至2020年间进行的回顾性观察研究,关注感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒的成人住院患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究分析了接受重症监护的成人患者医疗记录,这些患者被确诊感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒,采用回顾性观察方法评估一年内的死亡率发生率。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究报告称,接受重症监护的感染流感甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒或B病毒的成人患者中,一年内的死亡率发生率高达30%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将高死亡率发生率解释为成人重症监护患者中流感感染严重性的指标,强调了改进监测和管理策略的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现突显了对严重季节性流感患者进行长期结果监测的重要性,为未来的研究和公共卫生干预提供了依据。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究采用回顾性设计,且数据收集可能存在偏倚,因此存在一定的局限性;但证据强度较高,因为研究明确聚焦于目标流感病毒,并使用了定义明确地区的医疗记录。}}.{

title: CHO cell production of a single, enveloped VLP vaccine co-displaying SARS-CoV-2, influenza and RSV antigens
abstract: Abstract Concurrent circulation of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (IAV), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major public health concern, driving the need for multivalent, combined vaccines. Here, we report the generation of trivalent enveloped virus-like particles (eVLPs) co-displaying SARS-CoV-2 spike (S), influenza A H1, and RSV fusion (F) proteins produced in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. Using both transient and stable gene expression systems, we achieved intrinsic co-assembly of all three antigens within enveloped particles. Stable CHO eVLP expression yielded antigen volumetric titers of 48 ± 2 mg/L. A prefusogenic F variant showed superior expression and incorporation efficiency compared to wild-type F and prefusion-stabilized forms. The adjuvanted trivalent eVLPs elicited IgG responses against S, H1, and F, together with S- and F-specific T-cell responses and antibodies targeting the palivizumab-binding site II of RSV-F, a clinically relevant neutralizing epitope. Notably, the formulation provided complete protection against homologous A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8; H1N1) challenge in mice , supporting further evaluation of this CHO-derived platform for combined respiratory-virus vaccination.

title: Report of the National Influenza Surveillance Scheme, 2022–2023
abstract: This report describes influenza surveillance activities in Australia in 2022 to 2023. Data were extracted from several sources constituting the National Influenza Surveillance Scheme. Following the relaxation of public health and social measures which had been applied in Australia in response to the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic in 2020 and 2021, the influenza seasons in 2022 and 2023 were characterised by high activity overall, with 1.4 and 1.8 times the number of laboratory-confirmed influenza notifications than those of the 2015–2019 pre-pandemic five-year mean, respectively. There were differences in the timing of the 2022 and 2023 influenza seasons compared to most pre-pandemic years, with earlier season starts and earlier peaks (approximately six to eight weeks earlier than in pre-pandemic years). There was also considerable variation in the timing of peak influenza activity between the states and territories, particularly in 2023. Notification rates were highest in the 5–9 years age group, with rates in this age group about two and a half times as high in 2022 and three times as high in 2023 as the overall notification rate in the corresponding years. Influenza A(unsubtyped) comprised most notifications in 2022 and 2023. Of the remaining samples, influenza A(H3N2) was dominant in 2022; however, in 2023, there was substantial circulation of influenza B, which predominantly affected children and younger adults, and of A(H1N1). Sentinel surveillance supports the assessment that both the 2022 and 2023 influenza seasons were characterised by early, high activity. High notification rates were also reflected in increased sentinel hospital admissions with confirmed influenza in 2023, particularly among children. The burden placed on sentinel hospitals due to people admitted with influenza was moderate in 2022 but high in 2023. Severity, measured through the proportion of patients admitted to sentinel hospital intensive care units, was moderate in both years and consistent with historical estimates. Influenza was recorded as the underlying cause of death in 0.16% of all deaths that occurred in 2022, and 0.24% of all deaths in 2023. Overall, the 2022 influenza season had high activity with low-to-moderate severity, while 2023 had high activity with moderate severity.

title: Non-thermal plasma efficiently decontaminates sensitive materials from respiratory viruses
abstract: Introduction Heat- and moisture-sensitive porous materials such as plush toys, paper products, and foam are widely used in pediatric and healthcare environments but cannot be decontaminated by conventional liquid disinfectants, heat, or UV-based methods. This creates a need for alternative dry, non-thermal technologies. Non-thermal plasma (NTP) offers a promising approach for disinfecting such materials without compromising their integrity. Methods In this study, we assessed the virucidal efficacy of a prototyped NTP device on four clinically relevant respiratory viruses—Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Influenza A virus (IAV), human Adenovirus (HAdV), and human Rhinovirus (HRV)—applied to paper, plush fabric, and foam rubber. Results Material characterization by SEM and XPS demonstrated only mild surface oxidation and no structural damage following NTP exposure. Across all substrates, NTP treatment produced time-dependent reductions in viral infectivity. Maximum reductions ranged from 5.5–6.3 log 10 for SARS-CoV-2, 6.3–7.1 log 10 for IAV, 4.0–5.9 log 10 for HAdV, and 2.7–5.0 log 10 for HRV, depending on the virus-material combination. Enveloped viruses (SARS-CoV-2 and IAV) were inactivated more rapidly than the non-enveloped viruses HAdV and HRV, although all viruses were reduced to nearly or completely undetectable levels after 30–60 min of treatment. Several virus-material combinations exhibited biphasic inactivation kinetics characterized by an initial rapid decline followed by a slower phase of inactivation. Discussion These findings support that NTP could be an effective, residue-free, and material-preserving method for inactivating a broad spectrum of respiratory viruses on porous substrates incompatible with conventional disinfection. NTP thus might represent a valuable tool for safely reusing sensitive items in pediatric and clinical settings and reducing contamination risks where existing methods are impractical.

title: Urban Climatic and Health Impacts of Aerosols
abstract: Aerosols, also known as particulate matter (PM), strongly influence the climate and pose considerable risks to human health. As short-lived climate forcers, aerosols alter the Earth’s radiative budget by absorbing and scattering incident solar radiation, thereby affecting global and regional temperatures, atmospheric circulation, cloud formation, and precipitation patterns. From a public health perspective, exposure to particulate matter, particularly fine and ultrafine particles, has been associated with a wide range of adverse outcomes, including respiratory diseases, neurodegenerative disorders, and premature mortality. In addition, aerosols can transport pathogens and represent a critical pathway for the transmission of airborne infectious diseases. Despite contributing to only a small fraction of the total atmospheric aerosols, bioaerosols are important determinants of indoor air quality and the associated human exposure. In urban areas, the climatic and health impacts of aerosols are of particular concern because of the large population exposed to elevated PM pollutant concentrations. Urban aerosols comprise a complex mixture of particles originating from diverse sources, ranging from anthropogenic emissions, such as fossil fuel combustion, industrial activities, and biomass burning, to natural sources, such as biogenic, secondary atmospheric processing, and wildfires. Given the rapid pace of urbanization and growth of urban populations worldwide, understanding the optical properties and health impacts of urban aerosols is essential for developing effective regulatory and mitigation strategies to reduce the aerosol-related environmental and public health burdens. Light-absorbing organic aerosols, commonly referred to as brown carbon (BrC), are among the dominant light absorbers in the atmosphere. Conventional understanding of BrC limits its absorption to ultraviolet-blue regions of the spectrum and associates its sources predominantly with biomass burning. Recently, the discovery of dark BrC (d-BrC) in biomass burning emissions has spurred a reassessment of BrC’s contribution to global radiative forcing. Unlike the more commonly reported weakly absorbing BrC, d-BrC exhibits strong absorption extending into the near-infrared wavelengths. However, despite the prevalence of anthropogenic BrC emission sources globally, the occurrence and climatic significance of d-BrC in urban environments remain underexplored. In Study (1), we present observational evidence of d-BrC aerosols in Southeast Texas, a hub for petrochemical industries located at the intersection of continental and marine airmasses. Combined real-time and offline measurements revealed that over 80% of aerosol light absorption at blue and near-infrared wavelengths was attributable to non-black carbon aerosols, with d-BrC identified as a dominant contributor. Particle-scale electron energy-loss spectroscopy corroborated the strong absorptivity of these d-BrC aerosols, characterized by imaginary refractive indices of ~0.11 at 550 nm and ~0.06 at 1047 nm. The observed d-BrC particles were likely emitted as primary aerosols from non-biomass burning sources, particularly traffic-related emissions. These findings provide compelling evidence for the presence and climatic importance of d-BrC in urban atmosphere, extending its relevance beyond biomass burning and wildfire emissions, and highlight the need to incorporate d-BrC into regional and global aerosol-climate models. Beyond its climatic impacts, ambient air pollution has received increasing attention from its associative role in accelerating the development of neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Fine and ultrafine particulate matter, defined as particles with aerodynamic diameters less than 2.5 and 0.1 micrometers (PM2.5 and PM0.1), respectively, are of major concern because the small sizes enable them to deposit deeply into respiratory tract upon inhalation and facilitate their translocation into the brain. In Study (2), we investigated the effects of acute PM exposure on the early development of AD using in vivo mouse models. We developed a whole-body mouse exposure chamber with a custom-designed aerosol-dispenser inlet to rapidly establish and maintain uniform particle concentrations throughout the chamber, particularly at the mouse nose level. The chamber was integrated with high-temporal-resolution in vivo microdialysis, enabling continuous monitoring of the hippocampal amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptide level, a pathological hallmark of AD, while ensuring unrestricted mouse movement and thereby minimizing stress-related interference. Chamber characterization showed that particle number concentration reached steady state within 7-8 minutes of aerosol introduction and remained spatially uniform. Using this platform, APP/PS1 mice were exposed to pyrolyzed wood-derived organic particles (Pyrosol), representative of biomass burning emissions, and copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO), representative of vehicle brake-wear emissions, through five 2-hour inhalation exposures over three days. Hourly microdialysis measurements revealed that Pyrosol induced a rapid increase in Aβ40 levels, reaching more than three-fold of baseline level within 2 hours of the first exposure, but the responses declined over time. In contrast, the CuO produced a delayed but persistent Aβ40 rise, reaching ~3.5 times the baseline level after the fourth exposure (~33 hours). These results demonstrate the capability of the whole-body chamber-microdialysis platform to capture time-resolved neurobiological responses to inhaled pollutants and reveal that short-term PM exposures can disrupt Aβ homeostasis, providing mechanistic insight into air pollution-associated AD risks. In Study (3), we examined the neurotoxicity potential of a broader range of common urban fine and ultrafine PM constituents using in vitro mouse-derived Neuro-2a cells, focusing on cell viability and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). A diverse set of pollutants–including carbonaceous particles (black carbon), organic matter (9,10-phenanthrenequinone), transition metal compounds (copper (Cu), iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), and manganese (Mn) species), and inorganic salts (sulfates, nitrates, and ammonium)–was tested across graded concentrations to derive dose-response relationships and lethal concentrations corresponding to 50% cell death (LC50). Results showed large variability in neuronal cytotoxicity across different urban aerosol chemical compositions, with 9,10-phenanthrenequinone (9,10-PQN) exhibiting the strongest neurotoxicity, while the inorganic sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) showed minimal toxicity. For the transition metal compounds, insoluble metal oxides (CuO, Fe3O4, ZnO) showed higher toxicity than their soluble counterparts. The MMP measurements revealed that mitochondrial dysfunction often occurred at relatively high cell viability, suggesting it can serve as an early indicator of neuronal stress preceding overt cell death. Importantly, not all cytotoxic pollutants strongly reduced MMP, indicating that different PM constituents follow distinct mechanisms of neuronal injury. This study highlights strong composition-dependent neurotoxicity and mechanistic diversity of PM constituents, and emphasizes the need for composition- and emission source-specific regulatory and mitigation strategies to alleviate the health risks of atmospheric PM. In Study (4), motivated by the lack of standardized methods for sampling virus-laden aerosols in indoor environments, we evaluated the effects of different bioaerosol aerosolization and sampling methods on the structural integrity of airborne viruses. Using filamentous influenza A virus-like particles (VLPs) as a safe surrogate, we compared three nebulizers–Collison, Blaustein Atomization Modules (BLAM), and jet nebulizers–and three bioaerosol samplers–liquid spot sampler (LSS), SKC BioSampler, and wet cyclone. The BLAM and jet nebulizers preserved 12–21 % of filamentous structures, whereas the Collison nebulizer reduced the filament recovery to ∼10 % due to its higher-shear aerosolization mechanism. Among the samplers, the condensation-based LSS achieved the highest filament retention (~30%), whereas SKC BioSampler and wet cyclone sampler retained only ∼10 % and ∼7 % of filamentous VLPs, respectively, because of their higher flowrates, shear forces, and impaction stresses. Furthermore, we also investigated the influence of relative humidity (RH) on viral structure integrity. An elevated RH level (85 %) improved filament retention by ∼20 % compared with dry conditions (25% RH). These findings demonstrate that commonly used bioaerosol aerosolization and sampling techniques can substantially alter the viral morphology, potentially affecting the viability and infectivity of sampled viruses. This highlights the necessity for gentler methodologies to improve the accuracy of laboratory studies and environmental monitoring of airborne pathogens. Collectively, the research presented in this dissertation advances our understanding of the impacts of aerosols on climate, neurodegenerative disease risks, and airborne pathogen sampling. These findings contribute to improving the accuracy of aerosol-climate models, provide insights for developing regulatory and mitigation strategies to address environmental health risks, and inform approaches for monitoring airborne pathogens.

Fine and ultrafine particulate matter, defined as particles with aerodynamic diameters less than 2.5 and 0.1 micrometers (PM2.5 and PM0.1), respectively, are of major concern because the small sizes enable them to deposit deeply into respiratory tract upon inhalation and facilitate their translocation into the brain. In Study (2), we investigated the effects of acute PM exposure on the early development of AD using in vivo mouse models. We developed a whole-body mouse exposure chamber with a custom-designed aerosol-dispenser inlet to rapidly establish and maintain uniform particle concentrations throughout the chamber, particularly at the mouse nose level. The chamber was integrated with high-temporal-resolution in vivo microdialysis, enabling continuous monitoring of the hippocampal amyloid-beta (Aβ) peptide level, a pathological hallmark of AD, while ensuring unrestricted mouse movement and thereby minimizing stress-related interference. Chamber characterization showed that particle number concentration reached steady state within 7-8 minutes of aerosol introduction and remained spatially uniform. Using this platform, APP/PS1 mice were exposed to pyrolyzed wood-derived organic particles (Pyrosol), representative of biomass burning emissions, and copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO), representative of vehicle brake-wear emissions, through five 2-hour inhalation exposures over three days. Hourly microdialysis measurements revealed that Pyrosol induced a rapid increase in Aβ40 levels, reaching more than three-fold of baseline level within 2 hours of the first exposure, but the responses declined over time. In contrast, the CuO produced a delayed but persistent Aβ40 rise, reaching ~3.5 times the baseline level after the fourth exposure (~33 hours). These results demonstrate the capability of the whole-body chamber-microdialysis platform to capture time-resolved neurobiological responses to inhaled pollutants and reveal that short-term PM exposures can disrupt Aβ homeostasis, providing mechanistic insight into air pollution-associated AD risks. In Study (3), we examined the neurotoxicity potential of a broader range of common urban fine and ultrafine PM constituents using in vitro mouse-derived Neuro-2a cells, focusing on cell viability and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). A diverse set of pollutants–including carbonaceous particles (black carbon), organic matter (9,10-phenanthrenequinone), transition metal compounds (copper (Cu), iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), and manganese (Mn) species), and inorganic salts (sulfates, nitrates, and ammonium)–was tested across graded concentrations to derive dose-response relationships and lethal concentrations corresponding to 50% cell death (LC50). Results showed large variability in neuronal cytotoxicity across different urban aerosol chemical compositions, with 9,10-phenanthrenequinone (9,10-PQN) exhibiting the strongest neurotoxicity, while the inorganic sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) showed minimal toxicity. For the transition metal compounds, insoluble metal oxides (CuO, Fe3O4, ZnO) showed higher toxicity than their soluble counterparts. The MMP measurements revealed that mitochondrial dysfunction often occurred at relatively high cell viability, suggesting it can serve as an early indicator of neuronal stress preceding overt cell death. Importantly, not all cytotoxic pollutants strongly reduced MMP, indicating that different PM constituents follow distinct mechanisms of neuronal injury. This study highlights strong composition-dependent neurotoxicity and mechanistic diversity of PM constituents, and emphasizes the need for composition- and emission source-specific regulatory and mitigation strategies to alleviate the health risks of atmospheric PM. In Study (4), motivated by the lack of standardized methods for sampling virus-laden aerosols in indoor environments, we evaluated the effects of different bioaerosol aerosolization and sampling methods on the structural integrity of airborne viruses. Using filamentous influenza A virus-like particles (VLPs) as a safe surrogate, we compared three nebulizers–Collison, Blaustein Atomization Modules (BLAM), and jet nebulizers–and three bioaerosol samplers–liquid spot sampler (LSS), SKC BioSampler, and wet cyclone. The BLAM and jet nebulizers preserved 12–21 % of filamentous structures, whereas the Collison nebulizer reduced the filament recovery to ∼10 % due to its higher-shear aerosolization mechanism. Among the samplers, the condensation-based LSS achieved the highest filament retention (~30%), whereas SKC BioSampler and wet cyclone sampler retained only ∼10 % and ∼7 % of filamentous VLPs, respectively, because of their higher flowrates, shear forces, and impaction stresses. Furthermore, we also investigated the influence of relative humidity (RH) on viral structure integrity. An elevated RH level (85 %) improved filament retention by ∼20 % compared with dry conditions (25% RH). These findings demonstrate that commonly used bioaerosol aerosolization and sampling techniques can substantially alter the viral morphology, potentially affecting the viability and infectivity of sampled viruses. This highlights the necessity for gentler methodologies to improve the accuracy of laboratory studies and environmental monitoring of airborne pathogens. Collectively, the research presented in this dissertation advances our understanding of the impacts of aerosols on climate, neurodegenerative disease risks, and airborne pathogen sampling. These findings contribute to improving the accuracy of aerosol-climate models, provide insights for developing regulatory and mitigation strategies to address environmental health risks, and inform approaches for monitoring airborne pathogens.

title: Modelling assessment of the different paths of between-farm transmission of avian influenza HPAI in Northern Italy in 2021--2022
abstract: We propose a stochastic epidemic model to describe the spread of avian influenza in a network of poultry farms. We consider three main paths of infection transmission between poultry farms: from nearby farms, mainly through airborne diffusion; from farms belonging to the same company, through shared veterinarians, forage providers and similar; from undetected small farms or wildlife. From the parameter estimation, based on a modified Expectation-Maximization algorithm, we infer that approximately 63% of the farms were infected from nearby ones, with an infection force declining with distance; of these, more than one third belonged to the same company of the estimated infector. About 20% were infected from premises belonging to the same company but farther away than the distance threshold of 2 km; the remaining ones from wildlife or unidentified sources. These estimates have been validated by a comparison with genetic data, available for a subset of the farms: the genetic distance between two farms identified, with high probability, as an infector-infectee pair is much lower than between random pairs. These results may help in the implementation of tailored prevention and control measures for future outbreaks.

title: Mild Influenza-Associated Encephalitis with Predominant Neuropsychiatric Manifestations in a Child: A Case Report
abstract: Influenza-associated encephalitis (IAE) is a rare but serious complication of influenza infection, predominantly affecting children. While most reported cases present with moderate to severe neurological symptoms, mild and self-limiting forms remain underrecognized. We report the case of a previously healthy 9-year- old boy who presented with fever, lethargy, behavioral changes, and two episodes of nocturnal complex behavior concerning for seizures during the course of an influenza-like illness. Laboratory evaluations were notable for leukopenia and elevated D-dimer levels. Neuroimaging revealed a medial right temporal arachnoid cyst, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed mild pleocytosis with positive influenza A PCR. Electroencephalography was normal. The patient was managed with intravenous antibiotics, antiviral therapy, and supportive care. His symptoms resolved rapidly without neurological sequelae, and he made a complete recovery. This case highlights that influenza-associated encephalitis can present with mild, transient neuropsychiatric symptoms. It demonstrates that a positive respiratory influenza test does not preclude central nervous system involvement, underscoring the importance of cerebrospinal fluid analysis for diagnosis and to avoid unnecessary interventions

title: Extended dosing intervals enhance the durability of a self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against pandemic H5N1 influenza: a randomized, observer-blind, dose-finding Phase I study
abstract: Avian influenza poses a persistent pandemic threat, yet traditional vaccines face production delays. Self-amplifying mRNA (sa-mRNA) technology offers potential advantages, including rapid development, dose sparing, and enhanced, durable immunity. We evaluated ARCT-2304, a bicistronic sa-mRNA vaccine encoding H5N1 hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA), in a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial (NCT06602531). Healthy adults (N = 212) received two doses of ARCT-2304 (1.5, 5, or 12 mcg) or control/placebo on a 4- or 8-week schedule. Primary outcomes evaluated safety and reactogenicity (solicited/unsolicited/serious adverse events [AEs]) and immunogenicity (HA inhibition and NA enzyme-linked lectin assays 28 days post-second dose). Immunogenicity results were benchmarked using serum from a prior study supporting licensure of an H5N1 vaccine. ARCT-2304 was well-tolerated, displaying mostly mild-to-moderate, transient, dose-dependent solicited AEs, with no safety concerns identified. Two doses elicited robust HA and NA humoral responses. An 8-week interval yielded higher magnitude and greater durability than a 4-week schedule, with neutralizing and anti-NA antibodies remaining significantly elevated 6–7 months post-second dose. ARCT-2304 also induced dose-dependent, Th1-polarized T-cell responses peaking at Day 29. These findings support advancing sa-mRNA platforms for pandemic influenza preparedness. Here, the authors present a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial of ARCT-2304, a bicistronic self-amplifying mRNA vaccine against H5N1 influenza. The findings support a potential role for self-amplifying mRNA platforms against influenza.

title: Molecular detection of Swine Influenza A Virus (swIAV) and its association with selected management parameters in Macedonian commercial farrow-to finish pig farms
abstract: The aim of this study was to detect the presence and identify subtypes of swine influenza A virus (swIAV) in Macedonian commercial farrow-to-finish pig farms, and to investigate associations between swIAV detection and selected management parameters. Ten nasal swabs were collected from each of the three age groups, i.e. suckling piglets, weaned pigs and nursery pigs. Real-time reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to detect the presence of swIAV in swabs, and multiplex RT-qPCR was used to subtype swIAV. Swine influenza A virus RNA was found in 23 (20.2%) of the tested pooled samples and on nine (47.4%) of the pig farms. Large farms were more often positive in contrast to small farms (70% vs. 22.2%) and had significantly higher numbers of positive samples (P<0.01). Weaned pigs had the highest frequency of positive samples among all age categories and, compared to suckling piglets, weaners were significantly more likely to be virus-positive (P<0.05). The subtypes detected were categorized as H3huN2hu, H1pdmN1pdm and H1avN1av. Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) indicated associations between swIAV-positive results and large farm size, high replacement rate (≥40%), lower average parity (≤5), and a high number of weaned pigs (≥12). These findings highlight the importance of targeted vaccination strategies accompanied by proper implementation of studied management practices, in order to mitigate swIAV circulation in farrow-to-finish pig farms.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus infections in immunosuppressed adults <65 years old: a comparative analysis with Influenza and SARS-CoV2
abstract: ObjectivesRespiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) vaccine policies have varied globally since their approval in 2023. In the UK, policy has adapted in line with National evidence generation such that from Autumn 2026 at-risk persons [≥]65 years old will become eligible for vaccination. Immunosuppressed persons <65 years will still not be offered protection. The objective of this study is to investigate the relative burden of RSV infection by age and immunosuppressed status (IC). DesignRetrospective observational cohort study using routine healthcare data from North West London Integrated Care System. ParticipantsPatients with a confirmed diagnosis of a respiratory viral infection (RSV, Influenza A and B, SARS-CoV2) between October 2021 and July 2025. Main outcomes measuresPrevalence and severity of RSV infection in immunosuppressed persons <65 years old, and to provide a comparative analysis with Influenza and SARS-CoV2 in a sub-cohort tested using a 4-in-1 combined rapid PCR test. ResultsDuring the study period, 1226 patients were diagnosed with RSV of whom 596 (48.6%) were <65 years old. In 1091 patients with clinical data, 341 (31.3%) were IC. Fifty (9.9%) patients <65 years old had severe infection (ICU admission or death within 28 days of diagnosis), of whom 14 (28.0%) were IC. Proportionally, 16.7% of all RSV-associated deaths and 55.1% of all ICU RSV-admissions occurred in adult patients <65 years old. RSV accounted for 665 (10.1%) infections confirmed by 4-in-1 viral PCR testing. Eight-nine (13.4%), 172 (9.3%) and 448 (12.0%) patients with RSV, Influenza A and SARS-COV2 experienced severe infection, of whom 32 (36.0%), 82 (47.7%) and 156 (34.8%) were <65 years old respectively. Eight (25.0%), 20 (24.4%) and 52 (33.3%) of patients <65 years old with severe infection were IC. On adjusted analysis, having an immunosuppressive condition increased the odds of a severe SARS-CoV2 infection, OR (95% CI) 1.36 (1.08-1.71) but not a severe RSV or Influenza infection. ConclusionsSevere RSV infections occur in persons <65 years old, with a significant proportion of patients having an immunosuppressive condition. Urgent research is needed to investigate the potential benefit of extending the current UK RSV vaccine policy to protect younger immunosuppressed adults.

full_text: Article summary AI generated Healthcare workers (HCWs) in Côte d’Ivoire face significant risks from respiratory viruses like influenza and COVID-19, making their vaccination crucial for public health. This study found that while 67% of HCWs received the influenza vaccine and 84% received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine, concerns about vaccine safety, particularly for COVID-19, highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccine acceptance and coverage. Abstract Introduction Respiratory viruses like influenza and SARS-CoV-2 pose ongoing global health threats, especially within healthcare settings where healthcare workers (HCWs) face elevated risks of exposure. By late 2023, COVID-19 was transitioning from a pandemic to an endemic phase globally and within Côte d’Ivoire, with sustained transmission but reduced severity due to accumulated immunity and vaccination coverage. Despite the World Health Organization’s recommendation to prioritize HCWs for seasonal influenza vaccination, achieving optimal coverage remains a challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) such as Côte d’Ivoire.COVID-19 vaccines were introduced in Côte d’Ivoire in early 2021, with healthcare workers prioritized during the initial phases of the national vaccination campaign, followed by gradual expansion to the general population. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among healthcare workers in Côte d’Ivoire. Method This cross-sectional survey was conducted in November 2023 across two urban regions of Côte d’IvoireCôte d’Ivoire to assess HCWs’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding influenza and COVID-19 vaccination. A total of 1,454 HCWs were interviewed. Descriptive statistics, logistic regression, and chi-square tests were used for analysis. Results Findings revealed that 78% of HCWs perceived influenza as potentially leading to severe illness or death, while 95% held this view for COVID-19. Although 79% considered the influenza vaccine safe, only 58% felt the same about the COVID-19 vaccine. In terms of uptake, 67% had received the influenza vaccine in the most recent season, and 84% had received at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose. HCWs who had received an influenza vaccine before the COVID-19 pandemic were significantly more likely to have received both the most recent influenza vaccine and at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine (p < 0.001).
